name: Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor
author: SmartWpThemes

sections.description:
Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor lets you build Elementor headers, footers, single templates, archives, search results, 404 pages, and reusable blocks with display conditions.

Demo: View live demo

The free plugin also includes a focused Elementor widget library and a dashboard where individual widgets can be enabled or disabled. WooCommerce-dependent widgets are registered only when WooCommerce is active.

Free template types

The Free edition supports the following template types:

  • Header — build a custom Elementor header and assign it to the entire site or selected locations.
  • Footer — build a custom Elementor footer and assign it globally or conditionally.
  • Single content templates — create Elementor layouts for posts and supported public custom post types.
  • Archive — design archive layouts for supported WordPress archive contexts.
  • Search Results Page — create an Elementor template for WordPress search-result pages.
  • 404 Page — replace the normal theme 404 output with an Elementor-designed template.
  • Custom Block — build reusable Elementor content that can be inserted where supported, including through the Nexus template shortcode.

The Theme Builder works with supported public post types and public taxonomies when they meet the plugin’s targetable-content requirements. This allows compatible third-party content types to participate without hard-coding every post type into the plugin.

Display conditions and template assignment

Use simple assignment rules to control where each published template appears:

  • Display Location — choose where the template should appear.
  • Exclude Location — prevent the template from appearing in selected locations.
  • User Roles — show templates based on login state or WordPress role.
  • Priority — lower numbers win when multiple templates match.

Custom Blocks and template shortcode

Published Nexus templates can be reused with [netb_template id="123"]. Replace 123 with the published Nexus template ID. Custom Blocks provide reusable Elementor-built content for supported locations.

Widget management

Use Nexus Builder > Dashboard to enable or disable Nexus widgets. Disabled Free widgets are not registered with Elementor, and WooCommerce-dependent widgets are available only when WooCommerce is active.

Free Elementor widgets

The Free edition includes these Elementor widgets:

  • Site Logo — Displays your site logo dynamically in Elementor.
  • Page Title — Displays context-aware page and content titles dynamically.
  • Site Tagline — Displays the WordPress site tagline dynamically.
  • Site Title — Displays the WordPress site title dynamically.
  • Post Meta Info — Displays contextual post metadata in Elementor templates.
  • Breadcrumbs — Displays contextual breadcrumb navigation for WordPress content.
  • Copyright — Adds customizable copyright content to Elementor layouts.
  • Reading Time Count — Shows estimated reading time for supported content.
  • Search (Ajax/Normal Search) — Provides configurable Ajax or normal WordPress search.
  • Dynamic Counter — Displays manual or dynamic numerical counters.
  • Info Card — Creates flexible information cards with actions.
  • Social Share — Adds configurable social sharing buttons.
  • Static/Dynamic Table — Creates manual or dynamic data tables.
  • Interactive Card — Creates interactive cards with visual effects.
  • Post Grid — Displays queried WordPress content in responsive grids.
  • Advanced Progress Bar — Displays customizable progress indicators with values.
  • Animated Link — Creates styled links with configurable animations.
  • Logo Grid — Displays logos in flexible responsive grids.
  • Animated Heading — Creates headings with animated rotating text.
  • Navbar — Builds responsive navigation with branding and actions.
  • WooCommerce Categories — Displays WooCommerce product categories in configurable layouts.

Pro Theme Builder extension

Mega Menu template type

  • Mega Menu — Build reusable Elementor mega menu templates for advanced navigation.

Popup Builder template type

  • Popup Builder — Create Elementor popups with targeting, triggers, and visit controls.

Pro Elementor widgets

The Pro extension adds these Elementor widgets:

  • Testimonial — Displays testimonials from manual or dynamic content.
  • Video Player — Adds a configurable video player to Elementor.
  • Advanced Button — Creates advanced buttons with flexible content and effects.
  • Custom/Dynamic Tabs — Creates tabs from custom or dynamic content.
  • Custom/Dynamic FAQ — Creates FAQs from custom or dynamic content.
  • Post / Custom Timeline — Displays posts or custom content as timelines.
  • Post Gallery — Displays queried content in image-led galleries.
  • Countdown Timer — Creates configurable countdown timers for Elementor.
  • Comparison List — Builds structured feature, plan, or product comparisons.
  • Price Table — Creates customizable pricing and plan tables.
  • Custom/Dynamic Charts — Visualizes custom or dynamic data as charts.
  • Logo Carousel — Displays logos in configurable carousel layouts.
  • Dynamic Content — Queries and displays WordPress content dynamically.
  • Advanced Image Gallery — Creates flexible image galleries with advanced layouts.
  • Advanced Heading — Builds advanced headings with highlighted content.
  • Advanced Icon Box — Creates feature boxes with icons, images, and actions.
  • Post List — Displays queried WordPress content in flexible lists.
  • Mega Menu — Builds advanced responsive navigation and mega menus.
  • Offcanvas — Creates configurable slide-in offcanvas content panels.
  • Vertical Menu — Builds responsive vertical navigation menus.
  • Scrollnav — Creates navigation linked to page sections.
  • Changelog — Displays structured release and update histories.
  • Image Masking — Applies creative masking treatments to images.
  • Custom Carousel — Creates flexible carousels for custom content.

Pro WooCommerce Theme Builder widgets

Pro adds dedicated Elementor widgets for WooCommerce single-product and archive templates:

  • Woo single Breadcrumbs
  • Woo single Sale Badge
  • Woo single Product Title
  • Woo single Product Gallery
  • Woo single Product Price
  • Woo single Product Rating
  • Woo single Short Description
  • Woo single Add To Cart
  • Woo single Stock
  • Woo single Product Meta
  • Woo single Product Tabs
  • Woo single Description
  • Woo single Additional Information
  • Woo single Reviews
  • Woo single Upsells
  • Woo single Related Products
  • Woo single Product Navigation
  • Woo Archive Breadcrumbs
  • Woo Archive Title
  • Woo Archive Description
  • Woo Archive Products
  • Woo Archive Categories
  • Woo Archive Filters

Pro extended Elementor features

The Pro extension adds these Elementor-level features:

  • Dynamic Text Highlight — Highlights matching text with configurable visual effects.
  • Scroll Driven Motion — Adds scroll-responsive motion and visual effects.
  • Animated Gradient BG — Adds animated gradient backgrounds to Elementor elements.
  • Background Image Parallax — Adds scroll-based parallax movement to background images.

Getting started with Nexus Builder

A typical workflow is:

  1. Decide what part of the site you want to design, such as a Header or Footer.
  2. Create the corresponding Nexus template.
  3. Assign a Display Location, for example Entire Site.
  4. Add exclusions if certain pages should retain another template.
  5. Choose User Roles only when visitor-based targeting is required.
  6. Use Priority to control which template wins when rules overlap.
  7. Open the template in Elementor.
  8. Add normal Elementor widgets and/or Nexus widgets.
  9. Publish the template.
  10. Test the relevant pages on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

For reusable content rather than a site-level Header/Footer/Single/Archive assignment, create a Custom Block and use it where supported, including with the [netb_template id="..."] shortcode.

External services

Social Share connects to the selected sharing service only when used. Dynamic tables may load an administrator-provided CSV URL; the selected external provider’s terms and privacy policy apply.

Source code

Human-readable JavaScript and CSS are included in the plugin package under assets/js/ and assets/css/.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Elementor.
  2. Install and activate Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor.
  3. Open Nexus Builder > Dashboard to review and enable the Free widgets you want available in Elementor.
  4. Create a new Nexus Theme Builder template.
  5. Select the appropriate Template Type, such as Header, Footer, Single, Archive, Search Results, 404, or Custom Block.
  6. Configure Display Location rules to determine where the template should appear.
  7. Add Exclude Location rules if the template needs exceptions.
  8. Configure User Roles when the template should be limited by login state or WordPress role.
  9. Set Priority when multiple templates may target the same location.
  10. Edit the template with Elementor, design the layout, and publish it.
  11. Visit a matching frontend location to confirm that the published template is being selected as intended.
sections.faq:
Does the Free Theme Builder require Elementor Pro?

No. Elementor is required, but Elementor Pro is not required for the Free Nexus Theme Builder workflow or any widget listed in the Free widget section.

Is the Pro functionality locked inside the Free plugin?

No. Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor Pro is a separately distributed extension. The Free plugin contains and provides the Free functionality described in this readme. Pro registers its own additional widgets and features when that separate extension is installed and active.

Can I build more than headers and footers?

Yes. The Free Theme Builder also supports supported single-content templates, archives, Search Results, 404 templates, and reusable Custom Blocks.

Can I target a template to a specific page or post?

Yes, when the content is available as a supported target. Use Display Location to include the required content and Exclude Location to create exceptions.

Which rule wins if a location is both included and excluded?

The matching exclusion takes precedence over a matching display rule.

Can templates change according to whether a user is logged in?

Yes. User Roles can target all users, logged-in users, logged-out visitors, or individual WordPress roles.

What happens if multiple published templates match?

The eligible matching template with the lowest Priority number wins.

Can I reuse a template through a shortcode?

Yes. Published Nexus templates can be rendered with [netb_template id="..."] where shortcode output is supported. Replace the placeholder with the required template ID.

Can I disable Nexus widgets I do not use?

Yes. Use the widget controls in Nexus Builder > Dashboard. Disabled Free widgets are not registered in Elementor.

Does WooCommerce have to be installed?

No. WooCommerce is required only for WooCommerce-dependent widgets. The rest of the Theme Builder and non-WooCommerce widget library can be used without WooCommerce.

What happens if WooCommerce is not active?

WooCommerce-dependent widgets are not made available, while the other Nexus widgets and Theme Builder functionality continue to work.

What happens if the optional Pro extension is deactivated?

The Free Theme Builder and Free widgets continue to work. Pages or templates that contain Pro-only widgets should be reviewed before deactivating Pro because those widgets are supplied by the separate Pro extension.

Is Mega Menu part of the Free plugin?

No. Mega Menu is provided by the optional Pro extension. The dedicated Mega Menu Theme Builder template type is registered by Pro when the relevant Pro functionality is available.

Can I use Nexus widgets on normal Elementor pages?

Yes. Widgets that are enabled and registered can be used in Elementor wherever their normal requirements are satisfied; they are not limited to Theme Builder templates.

Are compatible custom post types supported?

The Theme Builder and query-based widgets can work with supported public post types and taxonomies where the plugin exposes them as compatible targets or sources. Availability can depend on the individual widget/template context.

Can I use the Search widget for live search?

Yes. The Free Search widget includes an optional Live Search mode with a configurable minimum-character threshold.

Can the Counter use dynamic values?

Yes. In addition to manual numbers, the Counter includes supported count sources such as post/content counts, user-role counts, and comment counts, depending on the selected configuration.

Can the Table display WordPress content dynamically?

Yes. The Static/Dynamic Table supports manual table data and supported dynamic WordPress query configurations. It also contains bounded remote CSV data handling where that data source is selected.

Does the plugin send usage data or require an external account?

The Free Theme Builder does not require an external account to use its included functionality. External Demo or Upgrade links are administrator-initiated links rather than requirements for using the Free Theme Builder.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4.1.4

  • Fixed responsive alignment for Site Title and Post Meta Info widgets.
  • Added responsive Search button visibility controls, hidden by default on tablet and mobile.
  • Fixed responsive circle sizing for Social Share and Advanced Progress Bar widgets.
  • Fixed Classic Grid WooCommerce Categories cards so responsive heights remain content-driven.
  • Updated Free release metadata for stable version 1.0.4.1.4.

1.0.4.1.3

  • Added Popup Builder information to the Free Upgrade to Pro comparison.
  • Expanded the Free readme with current Pro upgrade information for Popup Builder and WooCommerce Single/Archive Theme Builder widgets.
  • Updated Free release and localization metadata for stable version 1.0.4.1.3.

1.0.4.1.2

  • Stability release for the Free plugin following the latest WordPress.org review audit.
  • Hardened Elementor template metadata updates so request-driven changes run only through the verified save flow with nonce and capability checks.
  • Improved late escaping for generated Elementor/widget HTML while preserving valid rendered markup.
  • Refined WordPress.org metadata and external-service URL declarations for a more reliable review and installation experience.
  • Final review-readiness cleanup: tightened remaining generated markup escaping and removed avoidable output-suppression cases without changing widget behavior.

1.0.4.1.1

  • Stabilized the 1.0.4.1 release with the latest Free widget and Dashboard refinements.
  • Improved WordPress.org review compliance for asset enqueueing, request sanitization, dependency metadata, readable JavaScript/CSS source assets, external-service disclosure, and translation packaging.
  • Hardened request-shape validation and narrowed Dashboard extension-setting payloads before dispatching extension save hooks.

1.0.4.1

  • Enhanced fixes for the Navbar widget.

1.0.4

  • Maintained the Free Theme Builder core and complete Free widget library.
  • Improved template assignment, Elementor editor integration, frontend rendering, localization, responsive behavior, security, and performance.
  • Updated WordPress.org submission metadata and separated extension-owned template functionality from the Free package.
  • Expanded readme documentation for the Free Theme Builder, Free widgets, and separately distributed Pro extension functionality.

1.0.3

  • Added translation files for supported languages.
  • Improved internationalization and escaping.

1.0.2

  • Added the plugin translation template.

1.0

  • Initial release.
